name: Text Spacing
explanation: This criterion requires that no content or functionality is lost when a user overrides text spacing with their own custom CSS, up to certain values: line height to at least 1.5 times the font size, spacing after paragraphs to at least 2 times, letter spacing to at least 0.12 times, and word spacing to at least 0.16 times. The site doesn't need to provide these controls itself — that's a different, stricter AAA criterion. What this criterion requires is that the page's layout doesn't break when someone else's stylesheet applies this extra spacing: text shouldn't get clipped, overlap other text, or disappear. The usual cause of failure is containers with fixed heights combined with `overflow: hidden` around text — the box doesn't grow to fit the now-taller text, so content is cut off.
whoItAffects: People with low vision or dyslexia often rely on browser extensions or user stylesheets that increase line height, letter spacing, and paragraph spacing to make text easier to track and decode, since tighter spacing can cause lines to blur together or words to be misread. If a site's layout can't accommodate that extra spacing, these users lose access to content that gets clipped inside a fixed-size box, or encounter buttons that overlap and become impossible to use. This also affects people with certain cognitive disabilities who use increased spacing to reduce visual crowding, and anyone using OS-level text-spacing accessibility settings that apply the same kind of override site-wide.
howToTest: Install a user-stylesheet browser extension and add a stylesheet that applies the criterion's spacing values to all sites. With that stylesheet active, browse through the page's cards, buttons, and body text, looking for any text that gets clipped, overlaps other text, or disappears behind a fixed-size box — that's a failure. Also check that every control is still visible and operable, not hidden behind other content that didn't resize.

check.question: A user applies a custom stylesheet that increases line height, paragraph spacing, letter spacing, and word spacing per SC 1.4.12. A card component on the site has a fixed height with overflow:hidden, and the bio text inside now gets cut off. What is the correct fix?
choices: Nothing needs to change, since the site itself doesn't have to offer text-spacing controls
Make the card's height flexible (e.g. min-height instead of a fixed height) and remove the overflow:hidden clipping so the text can grow without being cut off
Reduce the font size inside the card so the text takes up less space
Add a 'Read more' link so the clipped text is available elsewhere on the page
